themes_detail.label: Door/Window Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Door and window-related 311 complaints spiked to 13 this week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,500% increase (z-score: 17.68)—suggesting a potential building safety, break-in, or weather-related emergency affecting multiple properties in South Beach/Dongan Hills.
evidence: 13 door/window complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 17.68 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Timing coincides with recent weather events (snow/ice complaints: 2,904 over 90 days) that may have triggered structural damage
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden spike—weather damage, break-ins, or construction-related issues?
Interview affected residents to understand scope and severity of door/window failures

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints surged to 69 THIS WEEK, up 165% from the 26-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.11), indicating a significant infrastructure failure affecting public safety and visibility across the district.
evidence: 69 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 26 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (+165%)
z-score of 5.11 indicates statistically significant spike
Street light condition already ranked #8 in overall 90-day complaint volume (363 total), suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Did recent snow/ice storms damage lighting infrastructure or is this a separate outage event?
Contact DOT to determine response timeline and which neighborhoods are most affected

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 300% increase from the 1-complaint weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.0), potentially signaling a building-wide HVAC failure, mold outbreak, or environmental hazard affecting resident health.
evidence: 4 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (+300%)
z-score of 6.0 indicates high statistical significance
Timing may correlate with appliance complaints spike (4 complaints last week, +540% from baseline of 0.6)
reporting_angles: Are these complaints concentrated in one building or scattered across the district?
Investigate whether heating system failures during cold weather are triggering both appliance and air quality issues

themes_detail.label: Appliance Failure Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Appliance-related complaints surged to 4 last week, a 540% spike from the 0.6-complaint weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.97), possibly indicating widespread heating system failures or defective equipment installations during winter weather.
evidence: 4 appliance complaints last week vs. 0.6 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (+540%)
z-score of 6.97 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Overlaps temporally with indoor air quality spike (4 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting related infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Focus on whether heating systems are failing in rental buildings, leaving tenants without hot water
Cross-reference with water system complaints (551 over 90 days) to assess whether boiler/heating infrastructure is compromised district-wide

themes_detail.label: Maintenance/Facility Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance and facility complaints jumped to 11 two weeks ago, a 389% spike from the 2.2-complaint weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.72), suggesting neglected public infrastructure or building maintenance backlogs affecting parks and community facilities.
evidence: 11 maintenance/facility complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.2 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (+389%)
z-score of 4.72 indicates statistically significant spike
Aligns with repeated community board budget requests for park maintenance and DPR facility upgrades
reporting_angles: Determine which parks or public facilities drove the spike—playgrounds, athletic fields, community centers
Connect to chronic budget requests showing residents repeatedly ask for maintenance funding year after year
